notes: Four new Bracket 4 decks to play against: averages of real Bracket 4 decks for Grand Arbiter Augustin IV, Etali, Primal Conqueror, Zur the Enchanter and Liesa, Shroud of Dusk.
Bots wait to use instant-speed spells and abilities until the moment they matter, instead of firing them off as soon as they can.
Bots no longer cast a counterspell just to set off a trigger of their own, such as Y'shtola's.
Each player's latest choice (a mode, a colour, a creature type, a card named) shows beside their name, through the turn after it was made.
Bots under Fatespinner no longer skip their own main phase with lands and spells in hand, and pick the same step again for a second Fatespinner.
Bots treat putting a permanent into its owner's library as removal: Wan Shi Tong, All-Knowing now aims at an opponent's permanent and gets cast.
Bots no longer make token copies of their own legendary creatures, which died to the legend rule at once (Echocasting Symposium).
Bots use Jace, Multiverse Architect's −3 when it's the better play.
A game no longer stops with an error at the end step after a token copy of Avacyn, Angel of Horror dies.
While deciding on a mulligan, the card under your mouse grows so you can read it, as cards in your hand do.
In a two-seat lobby, a bot can be taken out again, leaving its seat open.
Adding a bot, the deck list opens on the tab you last looked at.
The site now tells you when a new version is out, and this page lists what changed in each one.
"Order my triggers" stays on after you take a turn back.
A token copy goes to the player whose effect made it, even when the original has changed hands (Preston, the Vanisher; Spitting Image).
The graveyard and exile buttons glow while you can cast, play or activate something from there.
Delayed abilities and effects that last a while are listed beside a player's emblems.
A card everyone saw go into a hand stays face up for everyone.
The modes chosen for a spell are shown to the whole table, a permanent shows whose it is when owner and controller differ, and one that taps for an ability shows a tap symbol.
